$comment: Usage rules for color tokens. Values come from figma-variables.json; this file only says when to use what. Each semantic token's description is composed from its category, group and variant. Published to public/tokens/colors.json and public/llms.txt by `npm run tokens`.
rules: Use semantic tokens (var(--color-bg-*), --color-text-*, --color-icon-*, --color-border-*) in components. Never use primitives or hex values directly.
Primitives (--color-<family>-<step>) only define what semantic tokens point to; add or change a semantic token in Figma rather than reaching for a primitive.
Match the category to the property: bg-* for backgrounds, text-* for text, icon-* for icons, border-* for borders and dividers.
Text and icons placed on a danger, warning or success fill use the matching on* tokens (e.g. --color-text-danger-ondanger on --color-bg-danger).
Interactive states use the -hover and -pressed variants of the same token, never a different hue.
Dark mode: semantic tokens switch automatically inside [data-theme="dark"]; don't add separate dark styles.

primitives.description: Raw color scales from 100 (lightest) to 1000 (darkest). black and white are transparent scales (opacity steps); the others are solid. Some chromatic primitives have different values in dark mode.

families.black: Black at increasing opacity — overlays, shadows, and neutral text/icon tints on light surfaces.
families.white: White at increasing opacity — overlays and text/icon tints on dark or colored surfaces.
families.grey: Solid neutrals for surfaces, borders and disabled states.
families.orange: Accent orange (not yet used by any semantic token).

variants.secondary-hover: hover state of the secondary variant
variants.tertiary-hover: hover state of the tertiary variant
